title: The focus-directrix property of the parabola, stated without a square root
statement: For every p and every point P, P lies on the parabola x^2 = 4 p y -- the conic datum (1, 0, 0, 0, -4p, 0) -- if and only if the SQUARED distance from P to the focus (0, p) equals (P.y + p)^2, which is the squared distance from P to the directrix y = -p. Comparing squares is not a weakening of the classical statement: CPoint.distSq is the squared distance to the focus by definition, and the perpendicular distance from P to a horizontal line is the absolute value of y - (-p), whose square is (y + p)^2 with no absolute value left to interpret. The point of the square-free form is that CReal.sqrt is a limit construction the ring normalizer cannot see through, so the classical dist-to-focus equals dist-to-directrix form would need sqrt injectivity on the nonnegatives as an extra step; the squared form is a pure commutative-ring identity over CReal.Equiv and is discharged flat.

formal.statement: theorem CPoint.parabola_focus_directrix : ((x0 : CReal) -> ((x1 : CPoint) -> Iff (CPoint.OnConic (CPoint.Conic.parabolaFocal x0) x1) (CReal.Equiv (CPoint.distSq x1 (CPoint.mk CReal.zero x0)) (CReal.mul (CReal.add (CPoint.y x1) x0) (CReal.add (CPoint.y x1) x0)))))

evidence.supports: CPoint.parabola_focus_directrix is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement, and Kernel::axiom_footprint reports 0 assumed names.

notes: WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. It is stated over CPoint.Conic.parabolaFocal (x^2 = 4 p y), not over CPoint.Conic.parabola (y = a x^2), and the two are not interchangeable here: reaching the same statement from y = a x^2 needs the focus (0, 1/(4a)), hence CReal.inv, which is partial and would drag a PosBound witness for a through a statement that otherwise needs no hypothesis at all -- this one holds for every p including p ~ 0, where the parabola degenerates to the line x^2 ~ 0. It also does not say anything about the REFLECTIVE property of the parabola: that needs the tangent line, so either a derivative on CPoint or an explicit tangency-as-double-root definition, neither of which is in tree.
